significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, after controlling for sequence similarity, “convergent same-mechanism enzymes will cluster in a mechanism subspace despite low sequence identity, while divergent homologs will separate,” with mechanism abstraction strengthening across ESM-2 scale; this ordering constrains how representations should behave for two contrasting evolutionary relationships rather than merely establishing EC decodability. It establishes a representational phenomenon and residue-level grounding, not a causal account of how the model performs a biological function; nevertheless, distinguishing learned reaction chemistry from homology is consequential because protein-model evaluations such as FLIP (Dallago et al., 2021) and ProteinGym (Notin et al., 2023) identify distribution shift across sequence space as a central obstacle to interpreting apparent functional knowledge. True and false are distinguishable in principle, but the phrases “partially transcends homology” and “especially in larger models” lack a quantitative boundary, while the submission itself notes that a negative result may indicate probe weakness, so refutation would not decisively rule out mechanism representation. The topic-substitution check lowers the assessment from the highest bands: generic probing of scientific concepts would not earn this score, while the claim-specific convergence/divergence ordering is materially sharper than the topic-median EC-decoding hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handle is the “mechanism-vs-homology discriminability score,” supplemented by a “mechanism subspace”; the former is mainly a post-hoc diagnostic of whether an existing embedding separates chemistry from homology, although the latter could eventually support sequence-level mechanism annotation. After re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a qualitative relation—same-mechanism non-homologs should cluster more than different-mechanism homologs, and the abstraction should strengthen with scale—so more than a model-specific search procedure survives recalibration, but it does not specify transferable thresholds or establish prospective accuracy on “orphan enzymes.” Scope is principally ESM-2 sizes and curated enzyme-mechanism classes, with immediate uptake by protein-model and annotation researchers rather than a demonstrated tool for experimental enzymologists or catalyst designers. In the topic-substitution check, the broad scientific-representation topic alone would support only median reach; the contrastive score and cross-homology prediction add some reach, but not enough for the ex-ante practitioner-oriented 7–8 band.
